## 23010101 — Ball knob (machine handle)

Usually spherical component made of plastic or metallic materials, for inserting onto a cylindrical bolt or for screwing onto a bolt with an external thread or for screwing into an internal thread, which is used to carry out manual adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices

---

## 23010102 — Star grip (machine handle)

a palm grip is a type of control element designed for ergonomic handling, allowing users to exert force or control with the palm of their hand. This design facilitates a comfortable and secure grip, often enhancing user interaction with devices or machinery. Unlike other control elements such as buttons, which are typically operated with a finger touch, or bow-type handles that may require a specific hand positioning, a palm grip offers a broader surface area for engagement, making it suitable for applications requiring sustained pressure or manipulation. The palm grip is commonly utilized in various products to improve user comfort and operational efficiency.

---

## 23010103 — Bow grip (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which is similar in shape to an arc or the letter C and which is usually used with internal threads at the component ends for fastening to the element to be moved and with which operators can carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices or which is used to open and close flaps and doors

---

## 23010104 — T-grip (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which resembles the letter T in shape and is designed so that it can be plugged onto a cylindrical bolt or screwed onto a bolt with an external thread or has an internal thread for screwing in and with which operators can carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices

---

## 23010105 — Gripping tray / folding pull handle (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which can either be mounted recessed into a component surface or in which the handle element can usually be folded at a 90° angle and which is either provided with internal threads or through-holes for fastening to the mounting base and is used to enable operators to carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices or which is used to open and close flaps and doors

---

## 23010106 — Ledge handle (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which can be mounted on a component surface and which is either provided with internal threads or through-holes for fastening to the mounting surface and which serves to enable operators to carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices or which serves to open and close flaps and doors

---

## 23010107 — Ball handle / lever handle (machine handle)

Conical or spherically shaped component made of plastic or metallic material, which is designed so that it can be plugged onto a cylindrical bolt or screwed onto a bolt with an external thread or has an internal thread for screwing in and with which operators can carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices

---

## 23010108 — Handle with additional function (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, in any shape, which is designed so that it can be placed on a cylindrical bolt and with which a clamping action takes place on the bolt by a 90° rotary movement and with which operators can carry out adjustment and operating procedures on machines and devices

## 23010401 — Crank handle (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which is designed in such a way that at one end of the component there is a bushing with a bore to accommodate a usually cylindrical axle and at the other end, connected by a lever, a rotatably mounted handle with which the operator can carry out adjustment and operating operations on machines and devices by means of rotary movements

---

## 23010402 — Spoked hand wheel (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which is designed in such a way that in the center of the cylindrical component there is a bushing with a bore for receiving a usually cylindrical axle and the central bushing is connected by several spokes to a larger cylindrical outer ring with a handle usually rotatably attached to it, whereby operators can carry out adjustment and operating operations on machines and devices by means of rotary movements

---

## 23010403 — Solid hand wheel (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which is designed in such a way that in the center of the disc-shaped, cylindrical or concave component there is a bushing with a bore to accommodate a usually cylindrical axle and in the area of the largest outer diameter it is connected to a handle, which is usually rotatably mounted, enabling operators to carry out adjustment and operating operations on machines and devices by means of rotary movements

---

## 23010404 — Safety clutch hand wheel (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which has a fastening device in the center of the disc-shaped, cylindrical or concave component for receiving a usually cylindrical shaft and is connected in the area of the largest outer diameter to a usually rotatably mounted handle and on which a rotary movement can only be carried out by the operator if the component is also pushed in slightly axially at the same time as the rotary movement, so that the component and shaft come into engagement and whereby operators can carry out adjustment and operating operations on machines and devices by means of rotary movements

---

## 23010405 — Spider handle (machine handle)

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material, which is designed in such a way that in the center of the cylindrical component there is a bushing with a bore for receiving a mostly cylindrical axle and the central bushing has several spokes distributed around the circumference which simultaneously act as levers for exerting a rotary movement and whereby operators can carry out adjustment and operating operations on machines and devices by means of rotary movements

---

## 23010601 — Cam latchet

Mechanical component, predominantly made of metallic material, which can be fastened in holes in thin sheet metal and which is designed in such a way that it has a latching element at one end and a handle or a receptacle for a key at the opposite end, which can have different geometries and which serves to enable the opening and closing of flaps and doors by turning the key or handle, usually by 90°

---

## 23010602 — Spring-cam latchet

Mechanical component, predominantly made of metallic material, which can be fastened in holes in thin sheet metal and which is designed in such a way that it has a latch element at one end and a handle or a receptacle for a key at the opposite end, which can be of different geometric design and which serves to enable the opening and closing of flaps and doors by means of a usually 90° rotation of the key or handle, enabling flaps and doors to be opened and closed by turning the key or the handle, usually by 90°, and in which the latch simultaneously executes an axial movement during a rotary movement on the key or handle in order to ensure a reinforced locking of flaps and doors during a closing operation

---

## 23010603 — Indexing plunger

Mechanical component made of plastic or metallic material or a combination of both materials, which is designed in such a way that it has a cylindrical bolt at one end and a handle or a device for manual actuation at the opposite end and in which an axial movement of the bolt can be exerted via the handle and the cylindrical bolt can be locked in the disengaged position with a rotary movement exerted in addition to the axial pulling movement and which can be used to perform position locking on machines and devices

---

## 23010604 — Cam action indexing plunger

Mechanical component made of metallic material or a combination of metallic materials and plastic, which is designed in such a way that it has a cylindrical bolt at one end and a usually angled handle for manual actuation at the opposite end and in which an axial movement of the bolt is simultaneously exerted by a usually 180° rotational movement of the handle over an inclined plane, thereby disengaging the cylindrical bolt and which can be used to perform position locking on machines and devices

---

## 23010605 — Ball lock pin / Rapid release pin

Mechanical component made of metallic material or a combination of metallic materials and plastic, which is designed in such a way that it has a cylindrical bolt at one end, on the circumference of which usually two balls are resiliently embedded opposite each other, and which has at the opposite end a handle element of any design for manual actuation and in which the balls in the circumference of the cylindrical bolt can be unlocked by exerting pressure on the handle element via a mechanism and the balls can be locked by removing the pressure from the handle element and which serves to enable position locks to be made on machines and devices

## 23010701 — Leveling feet

Mechanical component made of metallic material or a combination of metallic materials and plastic, which is designed in such a way that it has a bolt with an external thread at one end and a larger, usually frustoconical or hexagonal, rigidly connected element at the opposite end, which serves to screw the bolt with the external thread into a suitable mating thread and the larger part in terms of surface area stands on a base and a height adjustment of machines and devices can be made by turning the bolt with the external thread

---

## 23010702 — Leveling mount

Mechanical component made of metallic material or a combination of metallic materials and plastic, which is designed in such a way that it has a bolt with an external thread at one end and a larger, usually frustoconical or hexagonal element at the opposite end. The bolt is designed in such a way that it has at one end a bolt with an external thread and at its opposite end a larger element, usually frusto-conical or hexagonal, which is pivotably and rotatably mounted on the externally threaded bolt and which serves to screw the externally threaded bolt into a suitable mating thread and the larger part in terms of surface area stands up on a base and, by rotating the externally threaded bolt, levelling and stabilization of machines, systems and devices can be carried out

---

## 23010703 — Leveling tube end

Mechanical component made of plastic, which is designed in such a way that it has a round, square or rectangular lamellar geometry on the outside at one end and a screw-mounted element with a flat contact surface at its opposite end and which serves to press the component with lamellar outer geometry into a geometrically matched profile tube and the screw-mounted element stands on a base and the height of furniture and appliances can be adjusted by turning the screw-mounted element

---

## 23020101 — Propeller shaft with length compensation

Machine element for the transmission of rotary movements that can expand axially to compensate for differences in the distance between connected components.

---

## 23020102 — Propeller shaft without length compensation

a specific type of mechanical component designed to transfer rotational motion and torque between different parts of a machinery or vehicle. This component is characterized by its inability to accommodate length variations and is typically employed in applications where fixed distances between connected shafts are maintained. It is constructed to withstand high levels of stress and fatigue, ensuring reliable performance in demanding environments. Distinct from similar components, this type does not feature mechanisms for length adjustment, setting it apart from other variations that include such functionalities. Its design is crucial for ensuring efficient power transmission in various machinery configurations.

---

## 23020103 — Double jointed propeller shaft

a flexible mechanical component designed to transmit torque and rotational motion between two misaligned shafts, allowing for angular movement while maintaining a connection. This type of shaft features two universal joints at either end, enabling it to accommodate variations in alignment and movement without compromising performance. It is particularly useful in applications where space constraints or significant angle variations occur, ensuring smooth operation and durability under varying load conditions. This classification is distinct from other types of propeller shafts that may focus on different methods of length adjustment or specific fitting configurations.

## 23020201 — Tubular shaft

a tubular shaft is a cylindrical component characterized by its hollow structure, designed to transmit torque or rotational motion in various mechanical applications. This type of shaft is typically used in scenarios where weight reduction is crucial, while maintaining strength and rigidity. It is distinguished from other similar components by its specific geometric profile and functionality, allowing for efficient energy transfer and support in systems where space and weight constraints are a consideration. Tubular shafts are commonly employed in industries such as automotive, aerospace, and manufacturing, serving as essential elements in drive systems, frameworks, and assemblies.

---

## 23020202 — Stub shaft

a stub shaft is a type of mechanical component characterized by its short length and specific design, typically utilized to connect or transmit power between other rotating elements within a machine or system. Unlike tubular shafts, which are elongated and hollow, stub shafts are solid and often feature a distinct form that allows for effective coupling with other components. They are commonly made from various materials to ensure durability and performance in demanding applications, including automotive, industrial machinery, and various engineering fields. The design and functionality of stub shafts make them essential for maintaining the integrity and efficiency of mechanical assemblies.

## 23020401 — Locking element (shaft-hub-connection)

a locking element designed to secure the connection between a shaft and a hub, ensuring stability and preventing relative movement between the two components. This element is utilized in various mechanical assemblies where precise alignment and reliable fixation are essential. The locking mechanism can vary in design and operation, distinguishing it from other fastening systems, such as internal or external locking configurations. The primary function of this element is to maintain the integrity of the assembly under operational conditions, thereby enhancing performance and safety in mechanical systems. It is an essential component in applications where rotational forces and loads are present.

## 23020402 — Internal locking system

a mechanism designed to secure and stabilize the connection between components, ensuring that rotational movement is effectively transmitted without slippage. This type of system is specifically intended for use within the confines of a housing or assembly, providing a reliable locking function internally. It is distinguished from other securing mechanisms by its integration within the assembly, offering enhanced protection against external forces that could compromise the connection. The design typically prioritizes ease of installation and maintenance, contributing to the overall efficiency and reliability of the connected components in various applications.

---

## 23020403 — External locking system

a mechanism designed to provide secure fastening or restraint between components, specifically utilized in applications where the connection must withstand external forces. This system typically features elements that engage from outside the primary assembly, ensuring stability and preventing unwanted movement or detachment. It is distinct from other fastening solutions that may rely on internal mechanisms or different locking approaches. The design is optimized for ease of installation and reliability in maintaining the integrity of the connection under various operational conditions.

a component designed to transmit rotational motion within a mechanical system, specifically for use in compressors. The design and dimensions are optimized for compatibility with compressor systems, ensuring efficient operation and durability under varying load conditions. It plays a critical role in maintaining the performance and reliability of the overall system.

## 23020601 — Rotor (compressor)

a component designed to facilitate the compression of gases, typically found in various mechanical systems such as engines or refrigeration units. This item is characterized by its ability to increase the pressure of a gas by reducing its volume, often through rotational motion. It is distinct from other similar components, such as turbine rotors, which are primarily used for energy generation or conversion. The design and functionality of this item are tailored to optimize performance in compression applications, ensuring efficiency and reliability in its operational context.

## 23020602 — Turbine rotor

a turbine rotor is a vital component in energy conversion systems, designed to rotate and transfer energy from fluid flow to mechanical energy. Typically found in applications such as power generation and propulsion, it operates by harnessing the kinetic and pressure energy of gases or liquids. The design and function of a turbine rotor distinguish it from other types of rotors, particularly those used in compression applications. Its efficiency, aerodynamics, and material composition are tailored to optimize performance under specific operating conditions, making it essential for the effective functioning of turbo machines.

## 23020701 — Flange joint

a flange joint is a mechanical connection that facilitates the joining of two components using a flat piece of material with holes for bolts or screws. This type of joint is characterized by its ability to provide a strong and secure connection while allowing for ease of assembly and disassembly. Flange joints are often utilized in various applications where the alignment and sealing of pipes or machinery are critical. They can accommodate thermal expansion and contraction, making them suitable for environments with varying temperatures. The design typically includes a gasket to ensure a leak-proof seal, enhancing the integrity of the assembly. Flange joints are widely used in industries such as manufacturing, automotive, and construction, where reliability and durability are paramount.

---

## 23020702 — Double joint

a device designed to connect two shafts while allowing for angular movement between them. This component is engineered to facilitate the transmission of torque and rotational motion, accommodating misalignments that may occur during operation. It typically consists of two or more articulating parts that can pivot relative to one another, enhancing flexibility and reducing stress on connected components. This type of joint is commonly used in mechanical assemblies where dynamic or variable alignment is necessary, ensuring smooth operation and longevity of machinery and equipment.

---

## 23020710 — Tolerance ring

a tolerance ring is a mechanical component utilized in the assembly of rotating shafts to facilitate precise alignment and mitigate the effects of misalignment between connected elements. This component is designed to enable controlled axial and radial movement, allowing for a certain degree of flexibility while maintaining structural integrity. Tolerance rings often feature a unique design that accommodates variations in manufacturing tolerances and thermal expansions. They play a critical role in enhancing the performance and longevity of shaft joints by reducing wear and friction, thereby improving overall efficiency in various applications across diverse industries.

---

## 23020711 — Balancing element

a balancing element is a component designed to stabilize and ensure the smooth operation of mechanical systems by counteracting imbalances in rotating machinery. It plays a critical role in minimizing vibrations and enhancing the overall performance and longevity of equipment. Typically used in conjunction with other mechanical parts, a balancing element contributes to efficient energy transfer and operational reliability. Its design and functionality are tailored to accommodate various applications, ensuring that the dynamic behavior of the system remains optimal under varying operational conditions.

---

## 23020712 — Cover (Rotor)

a protective or enclosing device designed to fit over a rotating element, typically used in mechanical assemblies to provide shielding, support, or alignment. This item serves to enhance the functionality or performance of the associated rotating component by preventing contamination, minimizing wear, or ensuring proper engagement within the assembly. It is distinct from other types of connections or joints that facilitate rotation or movement between parts, focusing specifically on the coverage aspect related to rotary mechanisms. This classification emphasizes the role of the device in maintaining the integrity and efficiency of rotational systems while differentiating it from other joint types that serve various connection or transfer purposes.

## 23020713 — Hub cap (pinion shaft)

this classification encompasses components designed to serve as protective or decorative caps specifically for the pinion shaft. These elements are integral in providing a finished appearance while also safeguarding the pinion shaft from environmental factors and mechanical wear. This classification distinguishes these components from other types of joints and connecting elements, focusing solely on the unique context of pinion shaft applications.

## 23020714 — Thrust collar

a component specifically designed to facilitate the connection and alignment of rotating shafts, ensuring the efficient transfer of torque and maintaining the integrity of the joint. This component is characterized by its ability to withstand axial loads and is often used to enhance the stability of the assembly. It plays a crucial role in various mechanical systems by preventing misalignment and providing support during operation. The thrust collar is typically manufactured from durable materials to withstand wear and tear, making it an essential part in applications where reliable performance is critical.

---

## 23020715 — Balance piston

a component designed to provide stability and equilibrium within a mechanical system, facilitating the smooth operation of rotating or moving parts. This element is typically integrated into assemblies where alignment and balance are critical for performance, ensuring that forces are evenly distributed. It may be utilized in various applications to mitigate vibrations and enhance the longevity of connected elements by reducing wear and tear. The design and functionality of this component differentiate it from other connection types, emphasizing its unique role in maintaining operational effectiveness within machinery or equipment.

## 23020716 — Blade lock

a blade lock is a fastening device specifically designed to secure components within a mechanical assembly, ensuring stability and functionality. It is typically utilized in applications where components must remain firmly in place under various operational conditions, such as vibration or torque. This device often features a mechanism that allows for easy engagement and disengagement while providing a robust locking system to prevent unintended movement. Blade locks are integral to maintaining the integrity of rotational assemblies and are commonly found in industries where precision and reliability are paramount. They differ from other fastening and joint types by their unique design and application focus, catering to specific needs in mechanical engineering and assembly.

---

## 23030901 — Face plate coupling

a face plate coupling is a mechanical device used to connect two shafts, allowing for the transmission of torque and rotation while maintaining axial alignment. This type of coupling typically features two flat plates that are bolted together, providing a rigid connection that is suitable for applications requiring high strength and precision. Face plate couplings are characterized by their ability to handle misalignment to a limited extent, while ensuring minimal backlash and high torque capacity. They are commonly employed in various industrial applications, including machinery, motors, and drives, where secure and stable shaft connections are essential for optimal performance and reliability.

## 23031403 — Mechanically actuated clutch

a mechanically actuated clutch is a device that facilitates the engagement and disengagement of power transmission between two rotating shafts through mechanical means. This type of clutch operates using physical components such as levers, springs, or gears, allowing for manual or automatic control of torque transfer. It is designed to provide reliable and efficient operation in various applications, ensuring smooth transitions between connected mechanisms. This classification is distinct from other types of clutches that utilize hydraulic, pneumatic, or electromagnetic systems, as well as those that engage through centrifugal forces or have overrunning capabilities. Mechanically actuated clutches are commonly employed in automotive, industrial, and machinery settings where precise control of rotational movement is essential.

---

## 23031404 — Hydraulically actuated clutch

a hydraulically actuated clutch is a device designed to engage and disengage power transmission in a mechanical system through the use of hydraulic pressure. This type of clutch operates by utilizing fluid dynamics to control the connection between driving and driven elements, allowing for smooth engagement and disengagement without the need for manual intervention. It offers advantages such as reduced wear, improved response times, and enhanced control over torque transmission. This classification distinguishes it from other actuation methods by focusing specifically on hydraulic mechanisms, differentiating it from those that rely on mechanical, pneumatic, or electromagnetic forces. Hydraulically actuated clutches are commonly utilized in various industrial applications where efficient and reliable operation is essential.

---

## 23031405 — Pneumatically actuated clutch

a device that utilizes compressed air to engage or disengage mechanical components, allowing for controlled transmission of torque between shafts or other rotating elements. This mechanism is designed to provide reliable operation in various applications where precise control and responsiveness are required. The function is achieved by manipulating air pressure to activate or deactivate the clutch system, enabling seamless transitions between engaged and disengaged states. This type of clutch is particularly advantageous in environments where rapid cycling and minimal physical force are necessary for operation, distinguishing it from other actuation methods that utilize mechanical, hydraulic, or electromagnetic principles.

---

## 23031406 — Electromagnetically actuated clutch

a device designed to engage and disengage mechanical systems through electromagnetic forces, facilitating the transfer of torque while allowing for rapid activation and deactivation. This type of clutch operates by utilizing an electromagnetic coil to create a magnetic field, which in turn moves a component to connect or disconnect the driving and driven elements. This mechanism offers benefits such as precise control, reduced wear, and the ability to function in environments where traditional mechanical linkages may be less effective. The device is distinct from other actuation methods, as it operates primarily on electromagnetic principles rather than mechanical, hydraulic, or pneumatic forces.

---

## 23031407 — Coupling (centrifugal, frictionally engaged)

a component designed to connect and disconnect shafts in a mechanical system through centrifugal force, utilizing friction to transmit torque. This device engages automatically based on the rotational speed of the driven shaft, allowing for smooth engagement and disengagement without the need for manual intervention. It is primarily used in applications where automatic coupling is advantageous, such as in certain engines and machinery, to enhance operational efficiency and reduce wear on components. The functionality is distinct from other actuation methods, focusing solely on centrifugal action as the primary mechanism for coupling engagement.

---

## 23031408 — Directionally actuated (overrunning clutch)

a mechanism that allows for the transmission of torque in one direction while preventing reverse motion. It operates by engaging when the input member rotates in the designated direction, effectively allowing power transfer, and disengaging when the direction of rotation reverses, thereby preventing backdrive. This type of device is crucial in applications where controlled motion and safety from reverse rotation are essential. Its design and function distinguish it from other types of engagement and disengagement mechanisms, which may rely on different actuation methods or operational principles. The directionally actuated mechanism is widely used in various machinery and automotive applications to enhance performance and reliability.

## 23040901 — Magnet brake

a magnet brake is a type of braking system that utilizes electromagnetic forces to create friction and stop or slow down the motion of an object. This technology is commonly used in various applications where precise control and rapid response are required, such as in transportation systems, industrial machinery, and safety devices. The operation of a magnet brake relies on the interaction between magnetic fields and conductive materials, allowing for smooth and efficient braking without the need for traditional mechanical components. This system is distinct from other braking technologies that rely on hydraulic, pneumatic, or manual mechanisms, offering unique advantages in terms of responsiveness and reliability in specific operational contexts.

---

## 23040902 — Hydraulic brake

a hydraulic brake is a type of braking system that utilizes hydraulic fluid to transmit force from the brake pedal to the braking mechanism. This system operates by leveraging the incompressibility of the fluid, which allows for efficient transfer of force, resulting in effective deceleration of a vehicle or machine. Hydraulic brakes are known for their smooth and responsive performance, making them suitable for various applications, including automotive and industrial machinery. This braking method is distinct from other types that rely on different mechanisms, such as magnetic, pneumatic, or manual systems, each with their unique operational principles and applications.

---

## 23040903 — Pneumatic brake

a type of braking system that utilizes compressed air to create friction and slow down or stop the motion of a vehicle or machinery. This system operates by converting pneumatic energy into mechanical force, engaging brake components that generate resistance against movement. Characterized by its efficiency in high-performance applications, it is commonly used in various transport and industrial settings where rapid response and durability are essential. This system differentiates itself from other braking technologies by its unique reliance on air pressure rather than electrical, hydraulic, or manual activation methods, making it suitable for specific operational environments and requirements.

---

## 23040904 — Manual brake

a manual brake is a mechanical device used to decelerate or stop the motion of a vehicle or machinery through direct human intervention. This type of braking system typically relies on physical components such as levers, cables, or rods, which the operator manipulates to create friction against moving parts, thereby reducing speed or halting motion. Manual brakes are characterized by their simplicity, ease of maintenance, and reliability in various conditions. They differ from other braking systems, such as those that utilize electromagnetic, hydraulic, or pneumatic principles, offering a distinct method of control and operation. Manual brakes are commonly employed in various applications where immediate feedback and direct control are essential.

## 23050101 — Dry friction bearing

a type of mechanical element designed to support and guide rotating or moving parts while minimizing friction through direct contact surfaces. This component operates on the principle of dry friction, where no lubricating fluids are used, relying instead on the properties of the materials in contact to reduce wear and ensure functionality. It is commonly employed in applications where high load capacity and durability are essential, often found in machinery and equipment that require reliable performance under varying operational conditions. The design and material selection are critical for optimizing performance and extending service life in its intended use.

---

## 23050102 — Aerodynamic bearing

a type of bearing designed to minimize friction and wear by utilizing aerodynamic principles to support loads. This component operates by generating a thin film of air between the bearing surfaces, allowing for smoother movement and reduced energy loss. Typically employed in high-speed applications, this bearing type enhances performance through the efficient management of airflow around the bearing surfaces. Its design is engineered to achieve optimal load-bearing capacity while maintaining stability and precision in motion. The aerodynamic bearing is distinguished from other bearing types by its unique operating mechanism and the specific conditions under which it functions effectively.

---

## 23050103 — Aerostatic bearing

a type of bearing that operates on the principle of a thin film of gas or air to support a load, enabling frictionless motion. This technology relies on the generation of a pressure differential created by the motion of the bearing surfaces, allowing for minimal wear and extended operational life. Aerostatic bearings are commonly used in applications requiring high precision and low friction, such as in aerospace, high-speed machinery, and precision instruments. These components are distinguished by their ability to maintain stability and performance under varying load conditions, making them suitable for environments where traditional bearing solutions may be inadequate.

---

## 23050104 — Magnet bearing

a type of bearing designed to provide support and reduce friction between moving components through the use of magnetic forces. This innovative solution eliminates the need for traditional lubricants, thus minimizing wear and extending the lifespan of the components. ## 23060502 — Cathodic corrosion protection

a method employed to prevent or mitigate the deterioration of materials, particularly metals, due to electrochemical reactions with their environment. This technique involves the application of a protective measure that employs a direct current, often through the use of a sacrificial anode or impressed current, to counteract the corrosive processes. It is typically utilized in various environments, including marine, underground, and industrial settings, to ensure the longevity and integrity of structures and components by reducing the rate of corrosion. This approach is distinct from other surface protection methods, focusing specifically on its electrochemical nature and application.

---

## 23060503 — Electro-chemical corrosion protection

a method or system employed to prevent or mitigate the deterioration of materials, particularly metals, due to corrosive processes through electro-chemical means. This approach involves the application of protective measures that create an electro-chemical barrier, enhancing the longevity and durability of the material by reducing the effects of environmental factors that contribute to corrosion. Typically utilized in various industrial applications, this protection method is distinct from other techniques like sacrificial anodes or surface coatings, focusing specifically on electro-chemical principles for effective corrosion inhibition.

---

## 23060504 — Zinc spray (surface protection)

a protective coating designed to prevent corrosion on metal surfaces, zinc spray serves as a barrier against environmental factors that can lead to deterioration. Typically applied using a spray method, this coating contains zinc particles that provide sacrificial protection, meaning the zinc will corrode preferentially to the underlying metal. It is particularly useful in applications where traditional paint systems may not offer adequate protection. The product is suitable for various surfaces and can be used in both industrial and domestic settings. Its effectiveness is enhanced by its ability to adhere well to surfaces, ensuring long-lasting protection against rust and oxidation.

These gaskets are distinct from other sealing solutions, such as bellow gaskets, due to their specific design and functional characteristics suited for particular applications.

This type of gasket is specifically engineered to accommodate pressure and prevent leakage of fluids or gases, ensuring the integrity of the connection it is sealing. Bellow gaskets are commonly utilized in various industrial applications where robust sealing solutions are required under dynamic conditions, differing from other sealing elements that may not possess the same flexibility or performance characteristics.

## 23100702 — Linch pin assortment

a collection of fastening devices designed to secure components in place by preventing axial movement. These items typically feature a cylindrical body with a head on one end that can be inserted into a hole to hold parts together, while the other end is often tapered or shaped to ensure a snug fit. The assortment includes various sizes and styles to accommodate different applications, providing versatility for assembly and maintenance tasks across multiple industries. This classification is distinct from similar fastening solutions, focusing specifically on the unique characteristics and functionalities of linch pins, which are utilized in a variety of mechanical and structural applications.

## 23120401 — Full rivet

Pin-shaped one-piece fixing element made of a metallic material, which has a head of any shape at one end and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120402 — Blind rivet

Pin-shaped two-part fixing element consisting of sleeve and mandrel, in which both components can consist of the same or different materials, in which the sleeve is formed with a head of any shape at one end and the mandrel has a predetermined breaking point, and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120403 — Compression rivet

Hollow-walled, one- or two-part fixing element in which one end of each part is formed with a head of any shape and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120404 — Riveting bolt

Pin-shaped, one-piece fixing element made of a metallic material, which has a cylindrical or conical depression centrally at one end in the axial direction and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120405 — Screw rivet

Fixing element which consists of a sleeve-shaped component and which has any desired head shape at one end into which a screw is tighten centrally in the axial direction in order to bring about a ductile deformation of the sleeve-shaped component

---

## 23120406 — Blind rivet nut

Sleeve-shaped fixing element made of a metallic material, which has any desired head shape at one end and which has an internal thread running in the axial direction in a partial region of the internal diameter and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120407 — Tubular rivet

Hollow-walled, one-piece fixing element in which one end is formed with a head of any shape and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120408 — Semi-tubular rivet

Pin-shaped, one-piece fixing element made of a metallic material, which has a cylindrical or conical depression in the axial direction centrally at one end and any desired head shape at the opposite end and which serves to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120409 — Expanding rivet

Fixing element which consists of a sleeve-shaped component which has any desired head shape at one end and into which a screw is tighten or a pin is driven centrally in the axial direction in order to cause the sleeve-shaped component to expand

---

## 23120410 — Self-piercing rivet

fixing element made of a metallic material, which has a conical or cylindrical recess in the axial direction centrally at one end and any desired head shape at the opposite end and which serves to be punched into two or more sheet metal components by a driving process in order to produce a component connection which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120411 — Lock Bolt

Two-part fixing element consisting of bolt and locking ring, in which the bolt has any desired head shape at one end and the shank of the bolt is usually profiled in the form of a groove, and in which the locking ring is tighten and pressed onto the profiled surface of the shank in order to produce a component joint which can no longer be detached without destruction

---

## 23120412 — Blind rivet screw

Fixing element consisting of a sleeve-shaped part in which a threaded bolt is captively inserted axially and which, by deforming the sleeve-shaped element, produces a no longer non-destructive component connection and at the same time the bolt thread serves as a means of fastening

## 23130101 — Turnbuckle

Component made of metallic material with internal threads, which has a right-hand thread at one end and a left-hand thread at the opposite end and is usually combined with joining elements such as hooks and eyes to hold two tension rods/ropes together by tensile stress. By turning the nut body clockwise or counterclockwise, the rods/ropes are tightened or loosened

## 23130111 — Calotte disc (steel construction)

## 23130201 — Wire rope

Rope consisting of a core, usually made of metallic wires or synthetic fibers, which is usually spirally wrapped by metallic wires combined into strands

## 23130202 — Fibre rope

Rope, with or without rope core in the middle of the rope, consisting of natural or synthetic fibers which are usually twisted or braided together into strands and in which several rope strands are combined or braided together

## 23130203 — Shackle (not for lifting purposes)

## 23130204 — Snap hook

## 23130205 — Shroud turnbuckle, Swage terminal

## 23130206 — Rope grip

Component made of metallic material, which is used to make eye connections or to connect two wire rope ends and which consists of several individual components that are geometrically shaped and mechanically arranged in such a way that they can be used to clamp ropes

---

## 23130207 — Rope thimble

Component made of metallic material, usually in the form of a loop, which is suitable for enclosing a rope in a semicircular shape around its circumference and which is used in conjunction with rope clamps to make eyelets at rope ends or to connect two wire rope ends

## 23130208 — Wedge socket (rope)

Hardware used to connect parts to a wire rope. The wedge and socket acts as a vice in securely gripping the rope. The wedge socket allows for quick and easy connections, but also allows the rope to be released when needed

## 23140101 — Hose clamp with worm gear drive

Clamps, for clamping connecting or joining parts of hoses, which are provided with a worm drive consisting of a smooth, embossed or perforated clamp band and a drive worm with any screw drive, which is mounted in a housing whose rotary movement acts directly on the clamp band

---

## 23140102 — Hose clamp with fastenig lugs

Clamps which are preferably used for fastening hoses to tubes and which are designed with clamping jaws and a one-piece or two-piece clamp band and which are designed with one or two clamping screws which are screwed into nuts through guide sleeves

---

## 23140103 — Bolt clamp

Clamp, for clamping connecting or joining parts on hoses and pipes, designed with captive round bolts on the smooth or V-shaped clamp band and one or two threaded bolts which are pivotably mounted in cross bolts and housings on the outside of the clamp band

---

## 23140104 — Screwless clamp

Clamp, for clamping connecting or joining parts of hoses and pipes, where the clamping effect is ensured by spring-elastic deformation of the clamp band or by mechanical deformation at one or more points of the clamp band or by mechanical engagement of the screwless closing mechanism

---

## 23140105 — Permanent band clamp

Smooth, embossed or perforated tape as a single component which, in conjunction with permanent band clamp closures adapted to the tape design, is used to fasten signs, containers or other components to pipes or profiles

---

## 23140106 — Permanent band clamp closure

Closure element used in conjunction with smooth, embossed or perforated endless tapes for fastening signs, containers or other components to tubes or profiles

---

## 23140107 — Fixing clamp

Fastening element made of metal or plastic, which usually consists of one or two semicircular elements and which is primarily used to clamp cables and pipes between the semicircular element(s) and which is designed in such a way that it can be fastened to another component by screwing or inserting it into an existing hole

---

## 23140108 — Block clamp

Fastening element made of metal or plastic, which usually consists of two semicircular elements and is mainly used in combination with a base and cover plate and which is mainly used to clamp cables and pipes between the semicircular element(s) and which is designed in such a way that the fastening element can be fixed on profiled rails or directly on a flat base with additional fasteners

---

## 23140109 — Steel strap for tube

Fastening element, mainly made of metallic material, produced from a round bar bent into a U-shape with at least one end threaded and usually used to clamp round ear profiles to another component

---

## 23140110 — Steel band hanger

Fastening element usually made of flat band-shaped material which is bent in a loop shape and whose ends are anchored in a second component and which serves to allow a pipe to be supported in the loop and in which the second component is such that fastening is possible preferably with a threaded rod to a substructure

---

## 23140111 — Beam clip

Component made of metallic material that can be clamped to flanges of beams and that is often used in conjunction with other components such as threaded rods or wire ropes to fasten cables or electrical components

---

## 23140112 — Cable tidy holder

Fastening element which is usually made of plastic and which is used to fix several lines or cables arranged next to each other to a substructure and which is designed in such a way that it can be fastened to the substructure with a usually pin-shaped fastening element

---

## 23140113 — Cable mount

Fastening element which is usually made of plastic and which is used to fix one or more lines or cables to a substructure and which is such that it can either be screwed to a substructure or glued to a flat substrate

---

## 23140114 — Dashpot

a mechanism designed to provide controlled damping through the use of a fluid medium, typically employed to reduce oscillations or vibrations in mechanical systems. This device is characterized by its ability to absorb energy and regulate motion, ensuring smoother operation and enhanced stability in various applications. The construction usually involves a cylinder containing a fluid and a piston or similar component that moves within the cylinder, thereby creating resistance to motion. This type of device is crucial in systems where precise control of movement is required, contributing to improved performance and longevity of the equipment it is integrated with.

---

## 23140115 — Variable spring hanger and variable spring support

a specialized support mechanism designed to accommodate variable spring hangers and variable spring supports, facilitating the secure attachment and stabilization of pipes, hoses, or tubes. This category encompasses components that allow for adjustable tension and alignment, ensuring flexibility in installation and maintenance. These items are distinguished by their capacity to adapt to varying load conditions and dynamic movements, providing a reliable solution for systems requiring adjustable support structures. The classification emphasizes products that differ significantly in design and functionality from standard fastening devices, focusing on those that specifically enhance the performance of variable spring applications within a broader framework of clamping solutions.

---

## 23140116 — Constant effort support

Device for suspending pipes that automatically compensates for changes in height due to temperature fluctuations and thus keeps the pipe in a constant position.

---

## 23140117 — Clamping plate

a clamping plate is a flat or shaped component designed to secure or hold items together, typically used in conjunction with other fastening devices to ensure stability and prevent movement. It is characterized by its function in providing a stable interface that evenly distributes pressure across the surfaces it engages. This component is commonly utilized in various applications where a secure connection is essential, particularly in mechanical assemblies, construction, and plumbing systems. Clamping plates are engineered to accommodate different sizes and types of fasteners, allowing for versatile use in diverse environments. Their design may include features such as holes or slots for bolts, screws, or other attachment methods, facilitating easy installation and removal.

---

## 23160102 — Aerial line fixture, -clamp, -connector (LV)

a type of equipment designed for the support and connection of aerial electrical lines at low voltage. This item is specifically engineered to secure and maintain the integrity of overhead power distribution systems. It includes various components that facilitate the attachment of conductors to support structures, ensuring reliable electrical connectivity while accommodating the specific requirements of low-voltage operations. The design and functionality of this equipment distinguish it from similar items intended for medium and high voltage applications, providing tailored solutions for safe and efficient power distribution at lower voltage levels.

---

## 23160103 — Aerial line fixture, -clamp, -connector (MV)

aerial line fixtures, clamps, and connectors designed for medium voltage applications provide essential components for the installation and maintenance of overhead electrical distribution systems. These items facilitate the secure attachment and connection of conductors to support structures, ensuring reliable electrical performance and safety. The devices are engineered to withstand environmental factors while maintaining optimal conductivity. Their design and functionality are distinct from those used in low voltage and high voltage applications, reflecting the specific requirements and operational conditions associated with medium voltage systems. These fixtures play a crucial role in enhancing the efficiency and durability of aerial line installations.

---

## 23160104 — Aerial line fixture, -clamp, -connector (HV)

aerial line fixtures designed for high voltage applications encompass various elements such as clamps and connectors that are specifically engineered to support, secure, and connect overhead electrical lines. These components are constructed to withstand the unique demands of high voltage environments, ensuring safety, reliability, and efficiency in the transmission of electricity. The fixtures are essential for maintaining the structural integrity of aerial installations, offering features that accommodate high voltage requirements while differentiating from those intended for lower voltage applications. Their design and materials are optimized for durability and performance in challenging outdoor conditions, contributing to the overall functionality of aerial power distribution systems.

---

## 23300901 — Planetary roller screw drive

a planetary roller screw drive features multiple short rollers that rotate around the central spindle, similar to a planetary gear system. the rollers engage the thread profile in sync, distributing the load over a large surface area. this enables high load capacities, smooth operation, and compact design. it is used where extremely high precision is required within a tight installation space.

---

## 23300902 — Roller screw drive with roller feed back

this version uses long rollers that are actively returned to their next position after each turn. the return is guided by mechanical paths inside the nut, allowing continuous, backlash-free motion under very high loads. it ensures smooth and precise movement even in heavy-duty and high-cycle applications. common in machine tools and industrial actuators for demanding motion profiles.

## 23301601 — Linear slider with plain bearing

a linear slide with plain bearing guidance uses sliding surfaces without rolling elements to achieve linear motion along a guide. this design is particularly robust, low-maintenance, and cost-effective. while it has higher friction than rolling systems, it offers simplicity and compactness. well-suited for dirty or low-precision environments.

## 23301602 — Linear slider with cam roller guide

## 23301603 — Linear slider with ball bearing guide

a linear slide with linear ball bearing guidance uses ball bushings that travel along hardened shafts. it enables smooth and precise motion with low friction, suitable for many standard applications. the design is cost-effective and easy to adapt. commonly used in handling systems, lab automation, or custom machinery.

## 23301604 — Profiled linear slider with rail guide

a linear slide with profile rail guidance runs precisely and backlash-free along a hardened rail with circulating balls or rollers. this type is known for high load capacity, repeatability, and long service life. it is used in demanding applications such as cnc machines, test systems, and precision axes. the structure is highly rigid and suited for heavy-duty conditions.

## 23310101 — Outer Taper (Driven Spindles)

a category comprising conical components designed to be attached to driven spindles, characterized by their outer taper shape. These components facilitate the secure connection of tools, ensuring optimal performance and stability during operation. The outer taper design allows for precise alignment and effective transmission of rotational force, making them essential in various machining and manufacturing processes. This category is distinct from other types of spindle attachments, such as those with inner tapers or cylindrical forms, and is specifically tailored to meet the requirements of applications where an outer taper configuration is necessary for efficient tool holding and operation.

The inner taper design offers distinct advantages in terms of stability and adaptability, allowing for efficient tool changes and enhanced performance in machining applications. It is differentiated from other configurations, such as outer tapers, cylindrical tool holding systems, and spindle extensions, by its unique design features and intended applications within driven spindle systems.

## 23320101 — Spur gear unit

a spur gear unit is a gearbox with parallel shafts using straight-cut spur gears. it transmits torque efficiently at medium to high speeds and features simple, low-maintenance construction.

---

## 23320102 — Flat gear unit

a parallel shaft gear unit has two or more parallel shafts in a compact, flat design. it is ideal for tight installation spaces and high torque transmission.

---

## 23320103 — Bevel gear units

a bevel gear unit is a type of gearbox used to transmit rotary motion and torque. it is characterized by input and output shafts that are positioned at an angle to each other, with their axes intersecting at a common point.

---

## 23320104 — Worm gear unit

a worm gear unit consists of a worm (screw shaft) and a worm wheel, enabling high gear ratios in a compact design. it may offer self-locking properties depending on configuration.

---

## 23320105 — Planetary gear unit

a planetary gearbox is a mechanical transmission system consisting of a central sun gear, several planet gears, and an outer ring gear.

---

## 23320106 — Turbo gear unit

a turbo gearbox is used to adapt rotational speed in high-speed applications such as turbines, compressors, or generators. it offers high precision, low losses, and thermal stability.

---

## 23320107 — Low-backlash gear unit

a low-backlash gearbox minimizes the play between input and output shafts to ensure precise positioning. it is used in automation, robotics, and machine tools.

---

## 23320108 — Speed change gear units

a shift gearbox allows manual or automatic switching between multiple gear ratios. it is used in vehicles, machinery, and test benches.

---

## 23320109 — Spindle gear unit

a screw jack gearbox converts rotary motion into linear movement using a trapezoidal or ball screw. it is suitable for lifting, lowering, positioning, and is often used in synchronized systems.

---

## 23320110 — Variable speed belt drive

a v-belt drive transmits torque through friction between a v-belt and pulleys. it is simple, cost-effective, and allows flexible shaft distances.

---

## 23320111 — Crown gear

a crown gear is a special type of gear and part of a crown gear drive. crown gear drives are used to transmit rotational motion and torque. a characteristic feature is the angled arrangement of the input and output shafts, whose axes usually intersect at a common point. power transmission occurs via a crown gear and a cylindrical gear, which distinguishes crown gear drives from bevel gear drives.

---

## 23320112 — Single-tooth thrust gear (Galaxie)

Gearbox type that makes use of linear sliding, realized through single thrust teeth and representing a kind of segmented planets. The movement of these individual teeth is returned to a centric shaft by a solid tooth carrier with radial holes for guiding the teeth

---

## 23320201 — Mechanical speed variators

a category of devices designed to alter the rotational speed of an input shaft, enabling precise control of output speed and torque. These mechanisms typically use mechanical components to achieve variable speed ratios, allowing for efficient adaptation in various applications. They are utilized in a wide range of industries to optimize performance, enhance energy efficiency, and improve the functionality of machinery and equipment. The primary function of these devices is to facilitate smooth transitions between different speed settings while maintaining the integrity and performance of the driven system.

---

## 23320202 — Hydrodynamic speed variators

hydrodynamic speed variators are mechanical devices designed to control the speed and torque of machinery by utilizing the principles of fluid dynamics. These systems typically operate through the use of hydraulic fluids to transmit power and adjust the rotational speed of an output shaft. They enable smooth acceleration and deceleration, providing efficient power transmission while minimizing wear and mechanical stress on components. The technology is commonly applied in various industrial applications, including manufacturing and transportation, where precise control of speed and torque is essential for optimal performance.

---

## 23320203 — Hydrostatic speed variators

hydrostatic speed variators are mechanical devices that utilize hydraulic fluid to transfer and adjust power and speed between a driving and driven component. These systems operate based on the principles of hydrostatics, allowing for smooth and precise control of speed and torque. The design typically includes pumps and motors that work in conjunction to vary the output speed according to the input speed, enabling efficient operation across a range of applications. Hydrostatic speed variators are distinguished from other types of speed alteration devices by their reliance on fluid mechanics rather than mechanical or hydrodynamic principles, making them suitable for environments where variable speed control and high torque at low speeds are required.

---

## 23330102 — Dispersion adhesive

Dispersion adhesives generally use water as mobile phase (dispersion medium), in which the adhesive components (eg, casein, thermoplastic or elastomeric polymer particles) are present as a dispersion. The water content is usually 40 to 70 weight percent. After application to the surface to be bonded, the dispersion breaks through escape of the dispersant in the joining parts or by the evaporation in the environment or by changing the pH value. The adhesive components converge towards it and form a film which can connect the two adherends

---

## 23330103 — Solvent-borne adhesive

In solvent-based wet adhesives, the polymer is dissolved in organic solvents, and is thus applied. The joining takes place at a point of time at which there is adequate solvent in the adhesive layer to ensure wetting of the second adherend surface. Through evaporation of the solvent the adhesive hardens, which means it is tough at first and eventually solidified by the formation of physical interactions between the polymer chains. Suitable solvents are, inter alia, esters (eg ethyl acetate), ketones (eg 2-butanone) or alcohols

---

## 23330104 — Hot melt adhesive

Hot melt adhesives - often also called 'hotmelts' - are solid at room temperature and are processed by melting. The hot melt glue is applied to the parts to be bonded and immediately joined to the second part within the open time. Immediately after cooling and solidification of the adhesive is the connection solid and functioning. This allows very fast cycle times in production processes and immediate further processing. For the hobbyist- and amateur users hot melt adhesives are available in form of glue candles (glue sticks) that can be processed with hot-melt glue guns. For technical applications, they are processed in the form of sheets, granules or blocks using melters and downstream hot-melt heads

---

## 23330105 — Cyanacrylate adhesive

Cyanoacrylate adhesives are generally better known as 'instant adhesive' or 'super glue'. These are about thin or intentionally thickened esters of cyanoacrylic acids, which are available in 1K-form as monomers and react to the actual adhesive polymer in the joint gap by polymerization reaction. Precondition for the start of polymerization, which leads to a hardening, is the presence of polar groups or particles, such as the OH-ions in the moisture layer on the adherend surface. It is an anionic polymerization, ie, nucleophiles, such as organic nitrogen compounds, sulfur compounds, or alcohols and water, affect the double bond at carbon atom polarized by the two strong electron-withdrawing substituents. This produces a mesomerism-stabilized anion, which affects the next monomer molecule in the further reaction progress. The polymerization is very fast, so that a solid compound prepared in seconds

---

## 23330106 — Single-component polyurethane glue

Polyurethane adhesives can be of 1 or 2 components. Polyurethanes cure by polycondensation or polyaddition. The one-component polyurethane adhesives cure with the addition of humidity and/or heat. It is possible to combine the two curing mechanisms, so that a first handling strength occurs by atmospheric moisture, the final strength of the bond occurs, but only under influence of heat. They play a role in means of transport for road/rail/air/water, as well as in shoe industry, glass processing, bindery, etc

---

## 23330107 — Two-component polyurethane glue

Polyurethane adhesives can be of 1 or 2 components. Polyurethanes cure by polycondensation or polyaddition. The one-component polyurethane adhesives cure with the addition of humidity and/or heat. It is possible to combine the two curing mechanisms, so that a first handling strength occurs by atmospheric moisture, the final strength of the bond occurs, but only under influence of heat. They play a role in means of transport for road/rail/air/water, as well as in shoe industry, glass processing, bindery, etc

---

## 23330108 — Single-component polyurethane-hybrid glue

a type of adhesive characterized by its unique formulation that combines properties of polyurethane and hybrid materials, designed to bond a variety of substrates effectively. This adhesive offers specific advantages such as enhanced flexibility, durability, and resistance to environmental factors. It provides a single-component solution, facilitating ease of use and application without the need for mixing. This category is distinct from other adhesive types that may utilize different chemical compositions or bonding mechanisms, ensuring targeted performance for specialized applications. Ideal for projects requiring strong and reliable adhesion, this product is suitable for both industrial and consumer uses, contributing to effective assembly and repair tasks across various materials.

---

## 23330109 — Epoxy resin adhesive

Epoxy resin adhesives - in short, epoxy adhesives - are made ​​up of two-component resin and hardener. As an epoxy polymer blocks are used to carry the so-called epoxy groups at the end. Usually the reaction products of bisphenol A and epichlorohydrin are used, which composes a stable thermosets after mixing with the hardener containing the amino or mercapto groups. The curing reaction can be carried out either at room temperature and at higher temperature. In this latter case usually higher strengths are achieved for the bond

---

## 23330110 — Structural adhesive glue (polymer base)

Structural adhesives are high performance adhesives with the greatest mechanical and chemical resistance and excellent adhesion on almost all the substrates. They are electrically and thermally insulating, and can be used in a variety of high-tech applications

---

## 23330111 — Anaerobic adhesive

This group of adhesives is used as a 1K system. The monomers of (modified) acrylic acid esters also cure by a radical chain mechanism similar to the methyl methacrylates. The special feature here is that the curing reaction only starts in the absence of oxygen (anaerobic) and in the presence of metal ions when the adhesive is concluded in a narrow metallic bond line from the ambient air

---

## 23330112 — Acrylate based adhesive

Two-component reactive adhesives in which the used monomer (methyl ester of methacrylic acid) is polymerized by a free-radical chain reaction. To start the polymerization reaction, a reactive radical is needed, which arises from a peroxide, when an accelerator is added. Enventually only to start the radical reaction, the 2-component system is needed, wherein the peroxide and accelerator come together and form the starting radicals. Both can therefore be commercialize: the peroxide in methyl methacrylate monomer as a component and the accelerator dissolved in the basic monomer as a second component. By mixing the two components, the radical chain reaction is initiated and the adhesive cures. Another variant brings the monomer and the peroxide into one component and uses as a second component only the accelerator. This allows the preceding mixing of the two components to be omitted (and the associated time), when the main component is applied to a joining part and the accelerator is applied on the other part

---

## 23330113 — Solvent-free adhesive

In solvent-free wet adhesives the polymer is dissolved in water, and is thus applied. The joining takes place at a point of time at which there is still enough water in the adhesive layer in place to ensure wetting of the second adherend surface. Through evaporation of the water the adhesive hardens, which means it is tough at first and eventually solidified by the formation of physical interactions between the polymer chains

---

## 23330114 — Pressure sensitive adhesive

Pressure sensitive adhesives are non-curing adhesives, which do not change their chemical state after completion of the adhesive mass (synthesis, partial cross-linking, etc.) until time of bonding, during the process of adhesion and in the application

---

## 23330115 — Contact glue

Contact adhesives (also called 'power glue') can be either solvent-based adhesives and dispersion adhesives, which are processed in the contact bonding process. As a bonding agent for this type of adhesive polymers are used (mainly polychloroprene and polyurethane), which merge after evaporation of the solvent after a certain period from the amorphous to the crystalline state, in which their strength is greatly increased

---

## 23330116 — All purpose glue cartridge

a type of adhesive specifically designed for general-purpose applications, typically packaged in a cartridge format for ease of use. This adhesive is formulated to provide a strong bond across a variety of materials, making it suitable for diverse tasks in both household and industrial settings. The product is characterized by its versatility, allowing it to be utilized in multiple environments, including construction, crafts, and repairs. The cartridge design facilitates precise application, minimizing mess and waste, and often includes features that enhance user convenience, such as nozzle attachments for detailed work. This adhesive type is distinguished from other adhesive formulations based on their chemical composition and intended use, offering a balance of performance and usability.

---

## 23330117 — Cartridge for reaction glue

a container designed to hold and dispense a specific type of adhesive that activates through a chemical reaction upon application. This product is typically used for bonding materials together and is characterized by its ability to form strong and durable connections. The adhesive within the container is formulated to cure through a reaction, often requiring specific environmental conditions or the presence of a catalyst to achieve optimal bonding performance. This type of adhesive is distinct from others based on its chemical composition and curing mechanism, making it suitable for particular applications where a robust and lasting bond is necessary.

---

## 23390201 — Flat strike plate

a flat strike plate is a flat, typically rectangular piece of metal or durable material designed to be installed on a door frame, providing a surface for the latch or bolt of a door to engage with when closed. Its primary function is to enhance the security of a door by preventing unauthorized entry and ensuring proper alignment of the door with the frame. Flat strike plates are characterized by their simplicity in design and are commonly used in various types of door hardware applications. They differ from other variations, such as angled or profile strike plates, in shape and functionality, catering to specific installation requirements and aesthetic preferences.

---

## 23390202 — Profile strike plate

a profile strike plate is a type of hardware component designed to enhance the functionality and security of door locking mechanisms. It is typically installed on the doorframe and serves as a reinforcement point for the latch or bolt of a door lock. Unlike other types of strike plates, this variant features a specific design that accommodates particular door configurations and lock types, ensuring that the locking mechanism engages securely and operates smoothly. Profile strike plates are utilized in various applications, including residential, commercial, and industrial settings, and are available in diverse materials and finishes to match different aesthetic and durability requirements. Their design allows for easy installation and compatibility with a range of door styles and lock systems.

---

## 23390203 — Angled strike plate

a specific type of fastening hardware designed to secure the alignment and functionality of a door or window latch. This component is characterized by its angular design, which facilitates the proper engagement of the latch mechanism when the door or window is closed. The angled configuration allows for enhanced stability and security, accommodating variations in installation and usage scenarios. It plays a crucial role in improving the overall performance of locking systems, ensuring a snug fit and reducing the risk of misalignment. This type of hardware is typically made from durable materials to withstand wear and environmental factors, making it suitable for both residential and commercial applications.

## 23400101 — Joist hanger (timber connection)

Sheet metal connector that is mainly used in structural timber construction to connect beams horizontally to other beams or to posts/columns and to transfer loads

---

## 23400102 — Beam hanger (timber connection)

Usually T-shaped metal component used in timber construction to connect beams invisibly horizontally to other beams or to posts/columns and to transfer loads

---

## 23400103 — Sleeper staple (timber connection)

Component made of flat steel, with pointed ends bent at 90° on both sides, which is used to be hammered into wooden beams of mainly truss constructions in order to connect them

---

## 23400104 — Wood-concrete bracket (timber connection)

Component made of flat steel, which is usually bent at a 90° angle and which is provided with holes to fasten the bracket to a wooden beam using screws on the one hand and to anchor the bracket in concrete using dowels on the other

---

## 23400106 — Cantilever bracket (timber connection)

Sheet metal component consisting of two individual parts, usually in mirror image, which is mainly used in structural timber construction to join two beams together at the longitudinal joint

---

## 23400108 — Cleat (timber connection)

Sheet metal connector used to fasten rafters to purlins using nails or screws

---

## 23400109 — Nail plate (timber connection)

Component made of sheet metal, with holes arranged in rows, which is used in structural timber construction to connect various wooden components to each other using screws or nails

---

## 23400112 — Post support (timber connection)

Metal component, with or without mechanical, vertical height adjustment option, which is provided on one side with an option for fastening to a foundation or for setting in concrete and on the opposite side with a fastening option for wooden posts

---

## 23400114 — Rafter shoe connector (timber construction)

Single or multi-part metal component used to connect rafters, in roof structures without purlins, to the abutment

---

## 23400116 — Bracing strap (timber construction)

Component made of strip-shaped sheet metal, with holes arranged in rows, which is used in structural timber construction to connect rafters diagonally across the width of a roof truss using screws or nails

---

## 23400117 — Angle bracket (timber connection)

L-shaped sheet metal part with one or more hole patterns that is used to connect wooden components in structural timber construction using nails or screws

---

## 23400121 — Beam anchor (wood connection)

T-shaped steel component used to connect gable walls and a wooden roof structure, usually at the rafters.

---

## 23400122 — Purlin anchor (timber connection)

Single or multi-part sheet metal fitting used in structural timber construction to connect rafters to purlins at their crossing point using anchor nails

---

## 23400123 — Inferior purlin anchor (timber connection)

Component made of flat steel with a splayed end that is used to be cast into a concrete ring beam and to which a wooden purlin can be attached to the ring beam at the protruding end

---

## 23400124 — Profile anchor (timber connection)

Component made of sheet metal that is shaped on one long side so that it can hook into the flange of a steel beam with an I or H flange shape or into a C-profile rail

---

## 23400125 — Tension tie (timber connection)

One or two-part metal component for use in structural timber construction, which can absorb horizontal and/or vertical loads in timber-concrete connections

---

## 23400126 — Dovetail connector (timber connection)

Two-part metal component used in structural timber construction to invisibly connect beam ends to each other or to connect a beam to another beam at right angles

---

## 23400127 — Rigid bracked (timber connection)

One-piece Sheet metal connector for connecting two overlapping beam layers that cross at a 90° angle

---

## 23400128 — Post corner connector (timber connection)

Shaped sheet metal part that can be placed over the end of a profiled timber with a square cross-section and to which one or more other geometrically identical profiled timbers can be connected at a 90° angle

---

## 23400129 — Fork shaped bracket (timber connection)

Sheet metal connector whose forked side can be placed over a beam and fastened to it and whose opposite side can be fastened to another beam crossing at a 90° angle above it

---

## 23400130 — Post cap connector (timber connection)

Two-part sheet metal fitting for connecting two overlapping beam layers that cross at a 90° angle

---

## 23400131 — Punched metal plate connector (timber connection)

Flat sheet metal part into which pointed teeth have been inserted at right angles to the nail plate contact surface and which is used to connect various timber trusses in a truss construction by pressing the teeth into the component surface

This motor is designed to maintain a constant speed under varying load conditions and is commonly used in applications requiring precise speed and position control. It typically features a rotor that is magnetically locked to the rotating magnetic field produced by the stator, which can be powered by alternating current. This type of motor is characterized by its efficiency and ability to operate at a specified speed determined by the supply frequency, making it suitable for various industrial and commercial applications.
